```text
# #4275: Patch: a smaller build of the C module for ports
Opened by @squishy-squooby.

Part of #2898. `crates/wasm/c` builds to about 43 MB (43,167,354 bytes on a recent build), and a port that translates it into another language carries every byte. Make it smaller without changing what it answers.

## What to try, measuring each

- `opt-level = "z"` (and `"s"`) for the module.
- LTO and `codegen-units = 1`.
- `panic = "abort"`. Check that a panic's text is still readable at `jackioh_result_ptr()` after the trap, as `crates/wasm/c/README.md` (Errors and traps) promises, with a test that proves it.
- `wasm-opt -Oz` when it's on PATH (skip it with a message when it isn't).
- Stripping the name section, if the size it saves is worth losing the names in a trap's backtrace.

`lto` and `panic` are profile-wide settings, so this likely means a custom profile, or a `[profile.release.package…]` override where one is allowed. Keep the built module at `target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/jackioh_wasm_c.wasm`, or say in the pull request what must change: CI's `web (wasm c module)` job reads that path, and workflows are outside the bot's paths.

## Done when

- `scripts/build-wasm.sh` (`JACKIOH_WASM_C=1 JACKIOH_WASM_NORMAL=0`) builds the smaller module and prints its size beside the old one's, raw and gzipped.
- The import section is still empty.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-wasm-c` and `crates/wasm/tests/export_parity.rs` pass.
- The pull request has a table of each setting's size and build time, and says which ones it kept.
- Nothing about the browser's module changes.

<!-- jackioh-bot:plan -->
## Plan

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/44603380618)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

Make the C module (`crates/wasm/c`, the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` cdylib a port translates, today ~43 MB) smaller without changing what it answers. The builder tries each setting from the issue (`opt-level`, LTO, `codegen-units`, `panic = "abort"`, `wasm-opt -Oz`, name-section stripping) one at a time, measures raw bytes, `gzip -9` bytes and wall-clock build time for each, keeps only the winners, and wires the kept settings into `scripts/build-wasm.sh` so `JACKIOH_WASM_C=1 JACKIOH_WASM_NORMAL=0 sh scripts/build-wasm.sh` builds the smaller module, prints its size, still imports nothing, and still leaves a panic's text readable at `jackioh_result_ptr()`/`jackioh_result_len()` after the trap. Nothing about the browser's module changes.

## Files to touch

| File | New / change | What changes there |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scripts/build-wasm.sh` | change | C-module block only: scoped `CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_*` env on the `cargo build -p jackioh-wasm-c` line for the kept settings; raw + `gzip -9` size echo; conditional `wasm-opt -Oz` with skip message; import-emptiness check moved after every transform; inline node check that a panic's text is readable after the trap |
| `Cargo.toml` | change only if needed | Only if a kept setting cannot be expressed as a `CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_*` env override on the script's build line (Cargo rejects some keys in `[profile.release.package.…]` overrides; the build error names them). Prefer no change here |
| `crates/wasm/c/README.md` | change only if needed | Only the Errors and traps paragraph, and only if a kept setting changes that promise (a stripped name section or `panic = "abort"` that still passes the readability check) |
| crates, apps it must not touch | — | `crates/wasm` (browser module), `apps/web`, `crates/engine`, `crates/cards`, `crates/ai`, `crates/run`, `crates/shared`, `crates/wasm/core`; no `spec/` note and no ruling (no rules decision is made); never `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, workflows |

Governing docs, not spec rules: `docs/v0.3.0/SURFACE.md` §10.5 (the C boundary contract) and `crates/wasm/c/README.md` (empty import section; Errors and traps). No spec section governs build size.

## Steps

1. Baseline. Run `JACKIOH_WASM_C=1 JACKIOH_WASM_NORMAL=0 sh scripts/build-wasm.sh`, then `wc -c` the module at `target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/jackioh_wasm_c.wasm` and `gzip -9 -c` piped to `wc -c`; copy it to `/tmp/jackioh_wasm_c.base.wasm`. Time the script's cargo line with `date +%s` before and after. Confirm the import check passes.
2. Build the probes (all in `/tmp`, nothing committed). A node script that, given a `.wasm` path, prints: import list (must be `[]`), export names, and the byte size of the `name` custom section (parse section id 0, read its name string; report 0 when absent). A second node script that instantiates the module with an empty import object, calls `init()`, dumps `constants()` and `catalog_version()` answers as JSON files; run it on the baseline and on every candidate, and `diff` the dumps (answers must be identical).
3. Establish the panic trigger on the baseline before touching any flag. Find one binding input that panics deterministically (start with `reduce` on a hand-made `{"type":"play", …}` whose body is not a `PlayAction`, aiming at the `expect` at `crates/engine/src/reduce.rs:257`; `create_game` and `fold` pre-validate setups in `crates/wasm/core/src/lib.rs`, so prefer inputs that pass those checks yet break an engine invariant). In node: `init()`, write the input via `jackioh_alloc`, call the export inside `try/catch`, expect an `unreachable` trap, then call `jackioh_result_ptr()`/`jackioh_result_len()` and read that many bytes from `memory`: assert non-empty UTF-8 containing the panic message. If post-trap calls fail even on the baseline, stop: the README promise does not hold as written, keep `panic = "unwind"`, and report this under Risks instead of proceeding with step 5.
4. Measure each setting alone, as a `CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_*` env prefix on a copy of the script's C build command (never exported, so the browser build is untouched): `OPT_LEVEL=z`, then `OPT_LEVEL=s`; `LTO=fat` (baseline profile is `thin`); `CODEGEN_UNITS=1`; `STRIP=symbols`. For each, record raw bytes, `gzip -9` bytes, wall time, import check, and the step-2 answers diff. Keep per-build notes; do not combine yet.
5. `panic = "abort"` last among the env trials (`CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_PANIC=abort`, alone first). Re-run the step-3 trap check against that build: keep `abort` only if the text is still readable and non-empty after the trap. If the hook no longer runs or the text is lost, drop `abort` and say so in the report. Native `cargo test -p jackioh-wasm-c` is unaffected either way (it uses the test profile).
6. `wasm-opt -Oz`: `if command -v wasm-opt >/dev/null 2>&1; then wasm-opt -Oz baseline-copy -o /tmp/c-opt.wasm` and record sizes, else `echo "build-wasm: no wasm-opt on PATH, skipping -Oz" >&2` and record the skip (it is absent on this machine; expect the same on CI). If it ran, re-run the import check and the answers diff on its output before believing its numbers.
7. Decide the name section from the step-2 measurement: strip it only if it costs on the order of megabytes (precedent: 5.6 MiB of 26.2 on the player module, noted in `scripts/build-wasm.sh`) and the step-3 text check still passes without it; otherwise keep the names and say the byte count in the report. Implement stripping with the tool that proved out in steps 4–6 (a kept `STRIP` value or the conditional `wasm-opt` pass), never by adding a new download to the script.
8. Compose the winners in `scripts/build-wasm.sh`'s C block, in this order: build line with the kept `CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_*` prefixes (one `VAR=value` prefix per kept setting on the `cargo build` command, with a comment naming each setting and its measured saving); conditional `wasm-opt -Oz` (skip message when absent); existing node import check unchanged but positioned after every transform; size echo printing raw and `gzip -9` bytes (mirror the CI summary lines); inline node trap-text check from step 3 that fails the build when the text is missing. Copy nothing to a new path: the module stays at `target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/jackioh_wasm_c.wasm`, so CI's `web (wasm c module)` job needs no change. If any kept setting forces a different output path, do not move it silently: leave the path as-is in the script and name the required workflow change in the report instead.
9. If and only if step 8 changed the Errors and traps promise (kept `abort`, or stripped names), update that paragraph of `crates/wasm/c/README.md`; otherwise leave the README alone. Update `Cargo.toml` only if step 8 proved a kept setting cannot be env-scoped.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p jackioh-wasm-c` — every C-boundary test in `crates/wasm/c/src/tests.rs` passes unmodified.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-wasm --test export_parity` — the C module still exports every browser binding plus only its memory interface, and still imports nothing from the host.
- `JACKIOH_WASM_C=1 JACKIOH_WASM_NORMAL=0 sh scripts/build-wasm.sh` — full C build with the kept settings: import check green, sizes printed, trap-text check green.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p jackioh-wasm-c --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- `cargo jackioh spec check` — proves no ruling or citation was disturbed (none is added).

## Done when

- [ ] The C-only build script invocation builds the smaller module at the unchanged `target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/jackioh_wasm_c.wasm` path and prints its raw and gzipped size.
- [ ] Each setting from the issue was tried with its raw size, gzipped size and build time measured, and the final report holds that table plus which settings were kept and why.
- [ ] The import section is still empty (script check and `export_parity` green).
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-wasm-c` and `export_parity` pass; answers are byte-identical to baseline (`constants()`, `catalog_version()` diffs empty).
- [ ] A check that runs on every C build proves a panic's text is still readable at `jackioh_result_ptr()`/`jackioh_result_len()` after the trap (or the report explains why `abort` was dropped).
- [ ] `wasm-opt` is used when present and skipped with a message when absent; nothing about the browser's module changed.

## Risks

- `panic = "abort"` may silence the hook that stows the panic text, or forbid unwinding a dependency relies on; the step-3 gate exists to catch exactly this, and the default is to drop `abort`, not the promise.
- Full LTO (`fat`) plus `codegen-units = 1` on a 43 MB module can push the build past CI's 20-minute `wasm-c` job timeout; a setting that does not fit in roughly 15 minutes wall time is dropped even if it shrinks the module.
- `opt-level = "z"` has precedent for hurting this codebase (the root `Cargo.toml` comment: `"s"` slowed the browser module's serde/state-cache path without shrinking it); runtime speed matters little here (the search is node-budgeted, `deadline_ms` is ignored) but size regressions are still disqualifying.
- Stripping the name section trades debuggability of trap backtraces for bytes; keep it unless the saving is measured in megabytes.

## Open questions

- None that blocks building: every setting is tried empirically, and each rejection criterion above says what to do when a trial fails. One judgment call remains for the reviewer: the exact size-vs-build-time tradeoff among the winning settings, which the report's table will lay out.
<!-- /jackioh-bot:plan -->
